newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Baoshan Steel pre-tax profit 4.97 bln yuan.
newsitem.headline: China's Baoshan Steel pre-tax profit 4.97 bln yuan.

text.p: Baoshan Steel and Iron (Group) Co, China's largest steel manufacturer, generated sales revenues of 27.22 billion yuan ($3.27 billion) in 1996 with pre-tax profits of 4.97 billion yuan, the Xinhua news agency said.
It achieved the profit in a year when foreign imports affected the market, Xinhua said in an overnight report quoting company chairman Li Ming. He gave no comparative figures.
The group's foreign currency earnings stood at $465 million, it said.
Baoshan Steel now had an annual production capacity of 6.5 million tonnes of steel, 6.71 million tons of iron, and 500,000 tons of seamless steel tubes, it said.
Through imports of advanced technology and strict control on staffin levels, the group has raised productivity to 655 tonnes of steel per capita annually, it said.

Unlike other large and medium-sized state enterprises, Baoshan Steel has no welfare facilities such as hospitals and schools for employees' families. All its auxiliary businesses, including equipment maintenance, have been hived off.
In addition, it moves about 2,000 workers a year to its subsidiaries, making Baoshan Steel China's top steel maker with the smallest number of workers in China.

Baoshan is engaged in an expansion project to increase steel manufacturing capacity by 4.29 million tonnes each year, and iron capacity by 3.25 million tons. The combined production capacity will reach 11 million tonnes by 2000, it said.
